chapter: Lecture 5: Weathering of Rocks and Minerals — Types, Physical & Biological Agents
subject: agricultural_chemistry_and_soil_science

questions.stem: Which of the following are recognized as the three fundamental processes of rock weathering in nature? (Select all that apply)
questions.rationale: Weathering operates via physical, chemical, and biological processes. Plate subduction is a deep crustal tectonic process. (Key Takeaway: The three fundamental weathering processes are physical, chemical, and biological.)

questions.stem: Which of the following are primary agents of Physical (Mechanical) Weathering? (Select all that apply)
questions.correct_answers: A, B, C, D, E (All options correct)
questions.rationale: Temperature cycling, frost wedging, hydraulic forces, wind abrasion, and lightning are all recognized physical weathering agents. (Key Takeaway: Physical weathering agents encompass temperature, frost, water, wind, and lightning.)

questions.stem: What secondary minerals are synthesized during the weathering of primary rock minerals? (Select all that apply)

options.B: Hydrous iron and aluminum oxides (Gibbsite, Goethite)

questions.rationale: Clays, hydrous oxides, and secondary carbonates are secondary minerals synthesized during weathering. Magmatic olivine is an unstable primary mineral. (Key Takeaway: Secondary minerals include clays, sesquioxides, and carbonates.)

questions.stem: Which organisms act as primary biological agents of rock weathering? (Select all that apply)

options.E: Deep-sea hydrothermal vent tube worms living on ocean ridges

questions.rationale: Plants, burrowers, termites/ants, and soil microbes are active terrestrial weathering agents. Hydrothermal vent worms do not participate in terrestrial soil genesis. (Key Takeaway: Terrestrial biological weathering is driven by flora, fauna, insects, and soil microbes.)

questions.stem: What mechanical changes are brought about by Physical Weathering? (Select all that apply)

options.A: Cracking and fracturing of rock boulders
options.B: Crumbling and crushing into gravel and sand
options.D: Alteration of silicate molecular chemical formulas

questions.rationale: Physical weathering causes mechanical fracturing and size reduction without altering mineral molecular chemical formulas. (Key Takeaway: Physical weathering causes mechanical size reduction with zero chemical formula alteration.)

questions.stem: Which of the following characteristics accurately describe Regolith? (Select all that apply)

options.A: It is an unconsolidated mantle of weathered rock debris
options.B: It rests above solid unaltered parent bedrock
options.C: It is formed through the combined physical and chemical breakdown of rocks
options.D: It consists of pure refined synthetic metal

questions.rationale: Regolith is the unconsolidated mantle of weathered rock residue resting above solid bedrock. It contains natural minerals, not synthetic metal. (Key Takeaway: Regolith is the unconsolidated weathered debris layer above parent bedrock.)

questions.stem: Which physical forces enable flowing river water to disintegrate bedrock? (Select all that apply)

options.A: Hydraulic impact and collision of moving water
options.B: Abrasive scouring by suspended gravel and sand bedload
options.C: Grinding of tumbling boulders along the riverbed
options.D: Complete dissolution of pure quartz crystals in seconds

questions.rationale: Hydraulic collision, suspended sand abrasion, and tumbling boulder grinding disintegrate river channels. Quartz does not dissolve instantly. (Key Takeaway: Hydraulic impact and sediment abrasion are the primary fluvial disintegration mechanisms.)

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about Exfoliation (Onion Weathering) are scientifically accurate? (Select all that apply)

options.A: Outer rock sheets peel away from the parent monolith
options.B: It is driven by differential thermal expansion between heated outer surfaces and cooler inner rock layers
options.C: It is common in massive Basalt and Granite rock outcrops
options.D: It occurs exclusively under permanent glacial ice sheets

questions.rationale: Exfoliation is thermal spalling of outer curved rock sheets in massive granite and basalt outcrops. It is not a subglacial process. (Key Takeaway: Thermal stress drives concentric exfoliation in massive granite and basalt.)

questions.stem: What roles do plant roots play in transforming rock into soil? (Select all that apply)

options.A: Mechanical root wedging into microscopic rock joints
options.B: Creating deep macropore channels for water percolation
options.C: Secreting biochemical organic acids that dissolve minerals
options.D: Preventing all chemical weathering from occurring

questions.rationale: Plant roots wedge joints open, create percolation macropores, and secrete corrosive organic acids. (Key Takeaway: Plant roots execute mechanical wedging, create percolation channels, and exude organic acids.)

questions.stem: Which living organisms are responsible for Pedoturbation (biological soil mixing)? (Select all that apply)
questions.correct_answers: A, B, C, D (All options correct)
questions.rationale: Termites, ants, earthworms, and burrowing rodents all actively mix soil and transport mineral particles vertically. (Key Takeaway: Pedoturbation is executed by termites, ants, earthworms, and burrowing animals.)
